why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-23 (phase-444 ledger re-read), gap -> declined. Two earlier passes each corrected the one before it; this one corrects the SECOND, and the prose it corrected is deleted rather than left standing above its own refutation.

UPSTREAM: `rcl_take_request_with_info` yields an `rmw_service_info_t` — the request id plus a `source_timestamp` / `received_timestamp` pair — alongside the payload.

OURS, MEASURED 2026-09-23: the IDENTIFYING half is there and the TIMESTAMPS are not. `nros_service_take_request_raw(service, buf, buf_len, int64_t *sequence_number)` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/detail/nros_generated.h:7459`) hands the sequence back and `nros_service_send_response_raw` requires it, which is what `rmw_request_id_t` is for.

WHY `declined` AND NOT `gap`: the ABI DECLARES the omission, so it is a decision, not an undone item. Of `take_request`, `packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_vtable.h:310-330` says `*seq_out` "stands in for `rmw_service_info_t *` — an RTOS reply needs the sequence and nothing else in that struct"; `take_response` (`:374-388`) carries the same declaration by reference. Neither slot has a timestamp out-parameter, so no backend is asked for one and none can offer one.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE 2026-09-21 PASS, both measured. (1) It cited the WRONG SLOT. `take_with_info` (`rmw_vtable.h:1046-1067`) is upstream `rmw_take_with_info`, the SUBSCRIPTION take; it is indeed `nullptr` in Cyclone (`packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/vtable.cpp:437`) and in the cffi table (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/lib.rs:281`), and none of that is evidence about a service. The service-side slots are `take_request` and `take_response`, and Cyclone FILLS BOTH (`vtable.cpp:341`, `:352`) — "no backend can supply them today" was true only because the ABI has nowhere to put them. (2) It cited `:7189` for `nros_service_take_request_raw`; the declaration is at `:7459`.

RE-OPEN IT if the ABI ever grows the pair: the item is a BACKEND one — a `*_with_info` out-parameter on the two service take slots — never an accessor written over a fact the seam does not carry. RFC-0089's frequency test also still answers no: `rcl_take_request_with_info` is reached from `rclc_executor` and from `rclcpp::Service`'s internals, both of which this campaign declines, and a user program takes a request through its callback.
